judges: Of The Meghalaya High Court. Before Coming To The J.
case_name: Zaffar Abbas Din Son Of Late Ghulam Nabi ... vs Nasir Hamid Khan Son Of Khwaja Hamid ...

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Zaffar Abbas Din son of late Ghulam Nabi Din, owner of a five-storeyed building known as 'Enso Tower'
parties.respondent_defendant: Nasir Hamid Khan son of Khwaja Hamid Ullah Khan, respondent who set up a supermarket mall/departmental store

facts_of_case: Petitioner owns a five-storeyed building. Respondent set up a supermarket mall/departmental store in the premises offered by the petitioner. Petitioner served notice to terminate the agreement due to unsatisfactory sales.

legal_principles.principle: A decision which is perverse or so irrational that no reasonable person would have arrived at the same requires some degree of explanation.
legal_principles.held: It is settled law that where: (i) a finding is based on no evidence, or (ii) an arbitral tribunal takes into account something irrelevant to the decision which it arrives at; or (iii) ignores vital evidence in arriving at its decision, such decision would necessarily be perverse.
cited_cases: H.B. Gandhi, Excise and Taxation Officer-cum-Assessing Authority v. Gopi Nath & Sons, 1992 Supp (2) SCC 312
Kuldeep Singh v. Commr. of Police, (1999) 2 SCC 10

legal_principles.principle: A court does not sit in appeal over the award of an Arbitral Tribunal by reassessing or reappreciating the evidence.
legal_principles.held: An award can be challenged only under the grounds mentioned in Section 34(2) of the Act. The Arbitral Tribunal has examined the facts and held that both the second respondent and the appellant are liable.
cited_cases: P.R. Shah, Shares & Stock Brokers (P) Ltd. v. B.H.H. Securities (P) Ltd., (2012) 1 SCC 594
